rationale: The Court will likely hold that § 106(a)’s express abrogation of “sovereign immunity,” read with § 101(27)’s definition of “governmental unit” to include any “foreign or domestic government,” unmistakably encompasses Indian tribes as domestic sovereigns, without requiring the words “Indian tribe.” A lone dissent (likely Thomas) will argue that Santa Clara Pueblo and Bay Mills demand a more tribe-specific clear statement and that generic catchall terms are insufficient to abrogate tribal immunity.
